question:
A 58-year-old man presents with right shoulder and arm pain following a direct impact sustained while
playing rugby. Examination reveals 4/5 strength in shoulder abduction and external rotation, with
forearm flexion maintained by stabilizing the elbow against his side. Shoulder adduction and forearm
flexion are normal, with no evidence of scapular winging. Biceps and triceps reflexes are intact
bilaterally, and sensation is unaffected. What is the most likely cause of his symptoms? Answer
Choices: (A) Brachial plexopathy (B) Brachial plexus injury (C) Spinal accessory nerve injury (D) Radial
nerve compression (E) Axillary neuropathy (F) Long thoracic nerve injury (G) Partial tear of the
infraspinatus muscle (H) Suprascapular neuropathy (I) Subacromial bursitis (J) Glenohumeral joint
dislocation
 A. Glenohumeral joint dislocation
B. Partial tear of the infraspinatus muscle
C. Long thoracic nerve injury
D. Axillary neuropathy
E. Brachial plexopathy
F. Brachial plexus injury
G. Spinal accessory nerve injury
H. Suprascapular neuropathy
I. Subacromial bursitis
J. Radial nerve compression
